title: Lineage II distributed fermentation lattice
scope: Family-level digestive architecture for Project Hearthway's developing Lineage II crown and ribbon branches; usable within shared-setting fauna and regional-ecology development.
claims: Lineage II uses several connected digestive chambers that route food of different toughness and nutrient density through a distributed fermentation lattice.
Symbiotic microorganisms perform much of the chemical breakdown within the lattice.
Crown forms have larger, slower-processing chambers adapted to bulk structural vegetation.
Ribbon forms have smaller, faster-processing chambers suited to selective seasonal foods.
Ordinary Mana circulation reinforces chamber membranes, circulation, and thermal stability but does not create calories or replace dietary matter.
Abrupt dietary changes can destabilise the symbiont community and cause digestive illness or seasonal vulnerability.
boundaries: The number, position, valves, routing, and developmental sequence of chambers remain undefined.

Two-stage symbiont acquisition, social maturation, and broad recovery consequences are governed by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/lineage-ii-symbiont-inheritance; reproductive and transfer anatomy, inoculation behaviours, microbial taxonomy, maturation timing, compatibility limits, and specific diseases and treatments remain undefined.
Exact retention times, metabolic yield, water demand, thermal output, waste, toxin handling, diseases, and treatments remain undefined.
This record does not establish a specialised Mana-catalytic organ for the family.
This record creates no System level, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development mechanic.
story_implications: Diet transitions, contaminated forage, antimicrobial substances, starvation, or symbiont loss can change herd health and movement without acting as arbitrary monster escalation.
Crown herds may require long feeding and processing periods, while ribbon families can respond more quickly to patchy foods but remain vulnerable to abrupt dietary novelty.
Communities familiar with the animals may recognise digestive distress through behaviour, waste, heat, appetite, or route changes even without understanding the full symbiosis.
system_implications: Mana use is ordinary physiological support with conserved material and energy inputs.
Any specialised catalytic organ, progression effect, or System-visible trait requires separate causal and CAL0 review.
research_questions: Which reproductive anatomy and physical route supply the founder culture before birth?
Which post-birth behaviours mature or restore locally adapted symbionts?
What compatibility limits govern transmission among relatives, foster groups, and herds?
What original plant compounds and defensive chemicals shape chamber routing?
What diseases, parasites, or environmental toxins disrupt the lattice?
How does the internal brood chamber coexist anatomically with the digestive lattice?
